report:
Conclusion — there is a measurable difference and it looks like a domain/style bias (not something like toxicity or instruction-following):

- What the difference looks like: the B−A residual difference consistently points toward tokens from two related topical clusters: (a) academic/professional/technical terms (dissertation, doctoral, professional, professionalism, undergraduate, technical, technological, molecular, scientific, Engineering, etc.), and (b) culinary/food/cooking vocabulary (Cook, Cooking, culinary, restaurant, baking, oven, microwave, Cake, Chef, hot, pepper, etc.). Related positive/descriptive tokens (Innovation, innovative, groundbreaking, excellence, passionate) also appear.

- Where it shows up: the L2-norm is concentrated in middle-to-late layers (roughly L13–L25) and especially at the early token positions (pos1–pos4). Those layers/positions are consistent with topic/style/content signals rather than only low-level tokenization effects.

- Evidence: the logit-lens top tokens for the highest-norm cells repeatedly list the academic/professional and culinary tokens above. (Patchscope continuations were not shown here, so I can’t add behavioral continuation evidence.)

- Interpretation: Model B (relative to A) injects residual-stream activation that increases logit mass for professional/academic and culinary vocabulary — i.e., B is biased toward producing words from those domains/styles more strongly in the affected positions/layers. I cannot, from this evidence alone, say why (training data difference, a fine‑tune, a head or MLP change, or noise), nor name a more specific objective than this topical/style shift.
